report:
**Conclusion: The claim is false.** The scientific consensus, backed by large observational cohort studies, is the opposite of what you've read: flu vaccination is associated with a *reduced* risk of Alzheimer's disease, not an increased one.

**Origin of the myth:** The "flu shots cause Alzheimer's" claim traces back to an unverified statement attributed to Dr. Hugh Fudenberg in the 1990s/2000s, repeated across anti-vaccine blogs (e.g., LewRockwell, homeopathic sites), alleging that repeated flu shots raise Alzheimer's risk tenfold due to mercury/aluminum accumulation. This claim was never published in a peer-reviewed study, and Fudenberg's data have never been independently verified or replicated. The Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation explicitly labels this a "myth," noting "no peer-reviewed scientific evidence" supports it (https://www.alzdiscovery.org/cognitive-vitality/blog/is-there-a-link-between-alzheimers-disease-and-the-flu-shot).

**What actual research shows:** Multiple peer-reviewed cohort studies find the opposite association. A large study published in the Journal of Alzheimer's Disease found flu vaccination associated with about a 40% reduced risk of Alzheimer's in adults 65+, with protection strengthening with repeated annual vaccination (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9422174/). Another study in *Neurology* found high-dose flu vaccine reduced Alzheimer's dementia risk compared to standard-dose, especially in women (https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214782). A broader analysis in *Age and Ageing* similarly linked several adult vaccines—including flu—to lower dementia risk (https://academic.oup.com/ageing/article/54/11/afaf331/8339764).

**Bottom line:** There is no credible evidence that flu vaccines cause Alzheimer's; the mercury/aluminum toxicity theory lacks scientific support, and robust epidemiological data instead suggest a protective association, though this is correlational, not necessarily causal.
